title: Player onboarding and first-session learning
summary: A tested path that helps a new player understand the experience promise, controls, first meaningful choice, and next goal.

principles: introduce one rule at a time
support skipping or recovery where appropriate
designKnowledge.privacy: Collect the minimum data needed for a defined learning question; use aggregate measures and an approved retention policy.

technicalPatterns.name: Design a first-session state map
technicalPatterns.guidance: Map entry, first cue, action, feedback, next goal, interruption, and returning-player path.

technicalPatterns.name: Test comprehension directly
technicalPatterns.guidance: Ask a first-time player to explain the goal and next action without coaching. Tutorial completion alone does not prove understanding.

dependencies.rationale: Hybrid experiences benefit from staged onboarding that introduces distinct loops and explains their connection.

failureModes.description: A long instruction sequence delays the first meaningful action.
failureModes.mitigation: Teach at the moment of use and validate comprehension in first-time playtests.

failureModes.description: The lesson assumes one input method or screen layout.
failureModes.mitigation: Repeat first-session tests on touch, gamepad, and keyboard/mouse.

scenarios.action: Observe first-time players on each supported device without verbal help.
scenarios.expected: Players can explain the experience promise, controls, and next action.

scenarios.action: Rejoin after interruption and test skip, resume, and replay behavior.
scenarios.expected: The player can continue without losing valid progress or being forced through irrelevant instruction.

acceptanceCriteria: Onboarding supports the primary gameplay loop.
Comprehension is observed, not inferred from clicks.
Analytics have an approved purpose and minimal retention.

considerations: Measure join time and first interactive response on the midrange mobile baseline.
Avoid loading large tutorial-only assets before they are needed.

sourceRefs.title: Approved Lab audience and product requirements

evidence.description: Onboarding principles, privacy boundary, failure cases, and repeatable first-session tests are defined.

assumptions: Audience, session length, and acquisition channels are hypotheses requiring research.
No player analytics are collected by this knowledge package.
